# The Doll (1938)

## Basic Information

**The Doll** (*Lalka*) is a Polish drama film released in 1938. It was directed by Michał Waszyński, one of the most prolific Polish directors of the interwar period.

## Source Material

The film is an adaptation of the novel **"Lalka"** (The Doll) by **Bolesław Prus**, published in 1887-1889. This novel is considered one of the greatest works of Polish literature and a masterpiece of 19th-century realism.

## Plot

The story centers on **Stanisław Wokulski**, a middle-aged Warsaw merchant and former political exile who becomes wealthy through trade. He falls deeply in love with **Izabela Łęcka**, a beautiful but shallow young aristocrat. The narrative explores themes of class differences, unrequited love, social ambition, and the clash between the declining Polish aristocracy and the rising merchant class in 19th-century Warsaw under Russian partition.

## Historical Context

This was one of the last major Polish films produced before World War II. The Polish film industry was devastated during the German occupation, making pre-war productions like this historically significant.

## Note

There have been other adaptations of Prus's novel, including a well-known 1968 television series directed by Wojciech Has.
